calls.head: The Golden Knights’ defense joins the attack, the Kings’ stays home
calls.body: The Golden Knights’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Kings’ not so much. Vegas is near the top of the league for shots from defensemen, and Los Angeles is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Golden Knights’ defensemen jump into the play.

surprises.head: Los Angeles’s shots went from harmless to more harmless
surprises.body: Los Angeles usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots, and Vegas is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Los Angeles’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 2.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 5.8% (about 5.5% against Vegas) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 150 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Marner ends it in overtime
paras: Trevor Connelly opened the scoring for the Golden Knights on the power play early in the second. Artemi Panarin made it 1-1 for Los Angeles on the power play less than four minutes later. Scott Laughton and Nic Dowd dropped the gloves midway through the second. Mitch Marner won it on the power play less than three minutes into overtime.
The Golden Knights owned the chances, outshooting the Kings 32-27, and still had to sweat it out in overtime. Carter Hart made 26 saves for the Knights, and Darcy Kuemper stopped 30 of 32.
The Golden Knights killed off a two-man advantage that lasted a minute and a half midway through the first. The Golden Knights moved to 5-1-0, and the Kings dropped to 0-2-2.

items.text: The Kings are 0-2-2, still looking for their first win.
Four straight wins for the Golden Knights.

Mitch Marner extended his point streak against Los Angeles to six games.
